functional.text: Search public posts by keywords, phrases and hashtags.
Two orders: 'Top' (relevance + engagement + recency) and 'Latest' (newest first), paginated.
Deleted or hidden posts disappear from results within ~1 minute.

non_functional.text: Search p99 < 500 ms, including ×5 spikes during big events.
A new post is searchable within ~10 s (near real time).
Available and horizontally scalable: data growth and query growth scale separately.

assumptions.text: 500M new posts/day, ~30 indexable terms each; 200M searches/day, ×5 during events.
5 years searchable; ~80% of queries only need the last 7 days.

out_of_scope.text: People search, typeahead, ads, personalisation by social graph, private posts.

api.notes: Cursor encodes the last (score, post_id) or time.
Owned by the post service; emits post-created event.

data.name: posts
data.fields: post_id (time-sortable), author_id, text, lang, created_at, visibility
data.why: Source of truth; the index can be rebuilt from it.

data.name: inverted index
data.fields: term → posting list of post_ids (newest first) + positions; per shard, per time tier; deleted-docs bitset
data.why: Maps words to posts without scanning; segments are immutable.

data.name: engagement signals
data.why: Changes constantly; read only for the top candidates.

deep_dives.title: Deletes and visibility changes in immutable segments

options.name: Rewrite the segment containing the post
options.cons: rewriting large segments per delete is far too expensive

options.name: Tombstone: mark the doc in a deleted-docs bitset per segment, filter at query, purge on merge
options.cons: deleted docs still take space until the next merge

deep_dives.choice: Tombstones in every tier's deleted-docs bitset, filtered at query time, purged on segment merge
deep_dives.why: Delete events reach all tiers within seconds through the same stream; F4's one-minute target is met without touching segment files.

deep_dives.title: Tail latency across hundreds of shards

options.name: Per-shard timeout, hedged request to a replica after p95, return partial results
options.cons: rarely misses a slow shard's hits

deep_dives.choice: Hedge to a second replica after the p95 latency and cut off at the deadline with partial results
deep_dives.why: With hundreds of shards, some shard is always slow; N1 matters more than the last few hits of a social search.

wrapup.bottlenecks: The real-time tier takes both the write burst and most queries during events (more replicas, separate indexing and query nodes); hot queries (short-TTL cache with coalescing); the slowest shard (hedging); indexer lag (scale consumers by stream partition).
wrapup.failures: Index nodes fail: replicas serve; a lost shard is rebuilt from segments or by replaying the post stream. Indexers down: the stream buffers and posts become searchable late. Signals store down: rank on text and recency only.
wrapup.monitoring: Search p50/p99 per tier, post → searchable lag (stream lag), shard error and timeout rate, partial-result rate, cache hit ratio, tombstone backlog.
wrapup.scale: More data → more shards per tier and new archive tiers on cheaper disk-heavy nodes; more queries → more replicas of the hot tiers; rebuild old tiers offline from the posts store.
wrapup.future: Personalised ranking (social graph, language), semantic/vector retrieval as a second candidate source, typeahead.

parts.title: Ingestion pipeline
parts.problem: Turn ~5.8k new posts/s (peak ~15k) and every delete into index updates within ~10 s, without slowing the post request or losing an update.

options.name: Post service writes to the index synchronously
options.cons: index latency and outages hit posting; dual write can diverge

options.name: Outbox/CDC events on a stream, indexer workers consume
options.pros: posting never waits; replayable; deletes travel the same path
options.cons: a few seconds of lag; one more system

parts.choice: Post created/deleted events via an outbox onto a Kafka stream; indexer workers tokenize and write to the real-time index
parts.why: The index is a derived view, so feeding it from a replayable log keeps it rebuildable and N2 is met with seconds to spare; partitioning the stream by post_id spreads ~15k/s across workers.

parts.title: Index partitioning and replication
parts.problem: Split a ~270 TB inverted index over many machines so that writes stay local, queries stay fast, and query throughput can grow separately from data size.

options.name: Term-partitioned: each shard owns a set of words
options.pros: a one-word query touches one shard
options.cons: one post writes to ~30 shards; hot terms melt one shard; multi-word queries join across shards

options.name: Document-partitioned: each shard owns a set of posts
options.pros: a post writes to one shard; shards are independent
options.cons: every query fans out to all shards of the tier

options.name: Document-partitioned inside time tiers, each shard replicated
options.pros: queries only touch tiers in their time range; old tiers are immutable and cheap
options.cons: tier boundaries to manage; a daily segment build

parts.choice: Document-partitioned shards inside time tiers (real-time, recent, archive), each shard replicated
parts.why: Most queries are about the last days, so the small real-time tier answers them; replicas scale the ~12k/s peak; immutable archive segments built daily are cheap to store and copy.

parts.title: Query fan-out and ranking
parts.problem: Answer ~12k queries/s at peak in < 500 ms when a query must reach every shard of the relevant tiers and the slowest shard sets the latency.

options.name: Query every shard of every tier and wait for all
options.cons: latency = slowest of hundreds of shards

options.name: Scatter-gather with per-shard top-k, timeouts and hedged requests
options.pros: bounded tail; returns partial results if a shard is slow
options.cons: results can miss a slow shard's best hits

options.name: Two-phase ranking: cheap per-shard score (text match × recency), broker re-ranks top ~1000 with engagement
options.pros: expensive features only on few candidates

parts.choice: Broker scatter-gathers to the tiers in the query's time range with per-shard top-k, timeouts and hedging, then re-ranks the merged top ~1000 with engagement signals; hot queries hit a short-TTL result cache
parts.why: Per-shard top-k keeps network small; hedging cuts the tail that hundreds of shards create; spikes are a few hot queries, which a 10–30 s cache absorbs without hurting N2.

parts.title: Recency: fresh posts and fresh signals
parts.problem: Make posts searchable within seconds and let likes and reposts (~60k/s) affect ranking, without rewriting index documents on every interaction.

options.name: Reindex the post document on every like
In-memory real-time tier refreshed every ~1 s + separate engagement signals store read at ranking
options.pros: new posts visible in seconds; signals update cheaply

parts.choice: In-memory real-time tier with ~1 s refresh for the last 7 days; engagement counts aggregated from a stream into a signals store that the broker reads for the top candidates
parts.why: The real-time tier is small (~2 TB) so it fits in RAM and answers 'Latest' with early termination in time order; batched signal counts keep ~60k events/s off the index.
